claim: Pure water boils at 100 °C (373.15 K) at a pressure of 1 standard atmosphere.

sources.label: Public introductory chemistry statement of the standard boiling point of water at 1 atm.
sources.provenance: Local educational example; not a live instrument reading.

interpretation: This is a scoped empirical convention under stated pressure, not a universal property of all aqueous mixtures or altitudes.
application: May be used for education. Must not authorize industrial process control without local measurement and qualified authority.

diamond.truth: The claim is limited to pure water at 1 atm; counter-evidence includes pressure change and impurities.
diamond.memory: Retain the pressure condition and the educational provenance of this example.
diamond.discovery: Local boiling temperature was not measured here.
diamond.understanding: Boiling point depends on pressure and composition.
diamond.wisdom: Hold as a textbook knowledge claim with uncertainty; do not treat as site instrumentation.

uncertainty: No local thermometer reading or laboratory certificate is attached.
correction_path: Qualify or retract if a cited standard or measurement disagrees.
unfinished_horizon: Mixture effects, altitude, isotopic composition, and instrument calibration remain out of scope.

viriditas.generative_effects: Supports basic scientific literacy without concealing pressure dependence.
viriditas.concealed_harm: None intended; overgeneralizing to unsafe process control would conceal risk.

authority.community_authority: Public scientific convention; no community-held restriction applies to this textbook statement.
